title: Make every reindex job keep its own partition

blocks.text: The search service rebuilds its index in partitions: `jobs(n)` returns one job per partition, and the jobs go to a pool that runs them in whatever order its threads pick them up, and runs a failed job again. After the last release, a 16-partition rebuild reindexed one partition sixteen times and left the other fifteen stale.

Finish `jobs(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Reindex.java`. When you're done, job number `i` reindexes partition `i`: whenever it runs, in whatever order, and as often as the pool runs it. About five lines in total.

cases.says: there is one job per partition, and running a job reindexes one valid partition
jobs run after all of them are built reindex every partition once, each its own
a job reindexes its own partition whatever order the jobs run in, and again the same one when it is run a second time

origin.section: Local Classes and Lambdas Capture Copies of Effectively Final Locals

concepts: Local and anonymous classes and lambdas capture copies of effectively final local variables; a shared mutable holder makes every capture read the same changing value.
